# Will I Miss It?

> "What fruit then did you have at that time in the things of which you are now ashamed?"
>
> — Romans 6:21

No.

The Little Monster starves, and the grooves the habit wore into your evenings grow over. The last scraps of the old lies go with them. You'll handle a hard day better than you do now. And the good days will be properly good, because you'll be there for the whole of them, with nothing to hide when you get home.

In the verse that opens this chapter, Paul didn't ask the Christians in Rome what they'd lost. He asked what they ever got. Go on, answer it. What fruit?

There's only one real danger left, and it's other men.

The world never stops telling a free man that he's the odd one. Sitcoms treat the habit as a harmless joke and "experts" call it healthy. Then one night you're on your own, a bit low, a bit lonely, and the thought arrives: *Everyone else gets to. Why not me?*

Look at how strange that thought is. Every man who never picked the habit up is glad he didn't. Every man who still has it wishes he'd never begun, and he'll tell you so after a couple of honest questions. Not one of them recommends it to his son. So who exactly are you envying?

It makes no difference which face of lust you look at. The man with the porn, the man with the hand and the man with a new woman every month are the same man. Not one of them is satisfied.

He doesn't approve of himself. If he knew you'd walked out, HE WOULD ENVY YOU.

## Who is doing without? {-}

The other reason a free man gets a twinge is simpler. The other man is *doing* something and you aren't, so it feels as if you're the one going without.

Turn it the right way up. You're not going without anything. He is. He is going without:

- Energy
- Drive
- Confidence
- A clear conscience
- Closeness to God
- Freedom
- Self-respect
- A word he can keep

He can't trust himself. You can.

Ask the men who've been out for a while whether they pine for it. One of them, hooked from twelve to twenty-one, wrote:

> "I've been freed now and it's nearly been 7 years."

He says his freedom came when God met him, and he describes what came with it: "this truly sensational feeling of peace for the first time in my life". That doesn't sound like a man missing his old hobby.

So drop the habit of envying men who are still in the trap. That isn't a sneer. Every free man was one of them once. You wouldn't envy a man who can't get through the day without a drink, however cheerfully he raises his glass. And like every trap of this kind, it doesn't stand still.

It tightens.

If he isn't enjoying it this year, he'll enjoy it less next year.

Don't envy him. Pity him, pray for him, and when the chance comes, hand him this book.
